purpose: Preserve exact service expectations and stable IDs for raw inputs that native controls cannot construct; actual native workflows and validation remain independent assertions. This is catalog review, not runtime coverage.

changes.reason: Replacement controls enumerate only active types with the same behavior; a wrong-behavior ID cannot be submitted through this control.
The type editor has no stable-key input and retains the existing key internally; this literal raw-key rename is an API boundary.
Type and priority stable keys are generated from the entered display name; the native editor exposes no raw taxonomy-key input.
The priority editor has no stable-key input and retains the stored key internally.
Default selectors enumerate scoped active choices; a foreign or retired raw default ID is not a native option.
The saved custom-field key input is readonly; the exact raw key-rewrite rejection belongs to REST/MCP.
The default editor constructs its discriminated value from the selected field kind and clears it on a kind change; it cannot submit a mismatched discriminator.
The choice picker exposes current scoped active option identities; raw foreign/missing option IDs cannot be selected.
This aggregate raw-input case includes missing generated IDs/revisions that the native option form never exposes. Native name/order validation is tested independently.
The native backfill action always requests a fixed bounded batch; there is no editable batch-size input.
The ready activation submit button is disabled until explicit confirmation. The exact confirm=false service request is not a native action.
Already-active projects show current mode and Open issues; they expose no repeat-activation submit action.
Both transition endpoint selectors enumerate only the selected workflow stages; a cross-workflow raw endpoint is not selectable.
The migration source selector enumerates closed stages only; an open source ID is not a native option.
Migration targets enumerate open active stages, while the selected source is closed; the source cannot be submitted as its own target.
Migration target options exclude retired stages; the raw retired target rejection is a service boundary.
Native checkbox and multi-select state contains unique field identities; it cannot construct a duplicate-ID policy.
The required-field picker reads only scoped project definitions; it has no input for an arbitrary foreign UUID.
The native required-field picker filters out retired definitions; a retired UUID cannot be selected as a new requirement.
The native policy command sets approverRole=null when count=0 and supplies the selected role for positive counts; incompatible raw combinations are service boundaries.
